props.title: Troma's War
props.initialSlug: Survivors battle mercenaries on deadly island

sections.content: **Troma's War** (1988) represents Lloyd Kaufman and Michael Herz's most ambitious and politically charged exploitation film. Following the massive success of The Toxic Avenger (1984), Troma Entertainment pumped nearly $3 million into this ultra-violent satire of Reagan-era militarism and action movies like **Rambo: First Blood Part II** (1985). The film follows plane crash survivors fighting against terrorists on a remote island, delivering Troma's signature mix of over-the-top gore, dark humor, and surprisingly sharp social commentary. While commercial failure nearly bankrupted the studio, it showcases peak Troma excess.

sections.content: The film's production history reveals Troma's ambitious reach exceeding their grasp. Originally titled "War and Peace," the MPAA forced multiple cuts to secure an R-rating, diluting its most extreme sequences. Still, **Troma's War** maintains the studio's anarchic spirit seen in earlier hits like **Surf Nazis Must Die** (1987) and **Combat Shock** (1986). The film's anti-war message comes through its excessive violence - a trademark of exploitation auteur Lloyd Kaufman's style that would influence later gore-heavy satires like **Natural Born Killers** (1994).

While mainstream critics dismissed it, **Troma's War** pioneered techniques that became standard in low-budget filmmaking. The guerrilla-style shooting, practical effects work, and mixing of genres influenced independent horror directors like Eli Roth (**Cabin Fever** [2002]) and James Gunn (**Slither** [2006]). The film's commercial failure forced Troma to scale back budgets, leading to their signature micro-budget style seen in later works like **Tromeo and Juliet** (1996). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

movies.title: Poultrygeist: Night of the Chicken Dead
movies.slug: Fast food workers battle zombie chickens in this musical horror-comedy. Peak latter-day Troma.

sections.content: Despite its initial failure, **Troma's War** has been reappraised as a key film in Troma's evolution. Its ambitious scope and political messaging paved the way for later socially conscious exploitation films like **Citizen Toxie: The Toxic Avenger IV** (2000). The film's influence extends beyond Troma, visible in modern genre-bending works like **Hobo with a Shotgun** (2011) and **Turbo Kid** (2015) that mix excessive violence with social commentary.
